title: Peter
lead: Simon, a fisherman from Galilee whom Jesus named Peter, "rock," was the first of the Twelve, the spokesman who confessed Jesus as Messiah and denied him, and a leader of the first church in Jerusalem. Christians still differ over what his place among the apostles means for the church today.

sections.b: All four Gospels put Simon first among the disciples and tell of his call, his confession and his denial (Matthew 16:13–20; Mark 8:27–30; Luke 9:18–21; John 6:68–69). Jesus gave him the name Kepha, Greek Petros, "rock" (John 1:42). After the resurrection the risen Jesus appeared to him first (1 Corinthians 15:5; Luke 24:34) and charged him to feed his sheep (John 21:15–19). In Acts he preaches at Pentecost and opens the church to Gentiles (Acts 2; Acts 10). Paul calls him one of the "pillars" in Jerusalem and once opposed him at Antioch (Galatians 2:9–14). Two letters bear his name, and early tradition says he died a martyr in Rome under Nero.
